title: Bulk or repetitive edits: write one script and run it with run_script
text: For many similar edits (every layer, a loop, generated layers or comps, keyframes in bulk, building a whole scene) write one After Effects style JavaScript and run it with the run_script tool instead of hundreds of tool calls. One script wrapped in app.beginUndoGroup / app.endUndoGroup is one undo step. Example: app.beginUndoGroup('x'); var c = app.project.items.addComp('Name', 1280, 720, 1, 5, 30); var s = c.layers.addSolid([0.2,0.8,0.4], 'Bar', 800, 28, 1); s.property('ADBE Transform Group').property('ADBE Scale').setValueAtTime(0.3, [0,100]); app.endUndoGroup(); c.numLayers

title: Shape layer operators (Round Corners, Offset, Merge, Twist, Zig Zag...) are values of layer.addShapeItem kind
text: There is no separate command per shape operator: add them with layer.addShapeItem {kind, layer?, group?}. Rounded corners: round (Round Corners). Grow or shrink an outline: offset (Offset Paths). Puffy or pinched edges: pucker (Pucker & Bloat). Swirl: twist. Zigzag or wavy edges: zigzag (Zig Zag). Union, subtract or intersect shapes into one: merge (Merge Paths). Gradient fill: gfill. Draw-on: trim, wobble: wiggle, copies: repeater (see their own notes). All kinds: group, rect, ellipse, star, polygon, fill, stroke, gfill, trim, repeater, round, offset, pucker, twist, zigzag, wiggle, merge.

title: A line that draws itself on over time: Trim Paths (layer.addShapeItem kind trim)
text: To make a shape layer line or stroke draw itself on, reveal gradually or grow from nothing to the full path, add Trim Paths with layer.addShapeItem {kind: "trim", layer} and animate its End from 0 to 100 (and Start for a travelling segment). Lighter and better for shape lines than the Write-on effect.
keys: draw a line on over time

title: Hand-drawn wobble and line boil on shape paths: Wiggle Paths (layer.addShapeItem kind wiggle)
text: To make shape layer lines tremble, wobble or boil as if drawn by hand, add Wiggle Paths with layer.addShapeItem {kind: "wiggle", layer}: small Size (1-3), Detail around 25, Wiggles/Second 0 and a stepped phase expression such as Math.floor(time*8)*97 so the line jumps a few times per second.

title: Copies of a shape in a row, a grid or around a circle: Repeater (layer.addShapeItem kind repeater)
text: To duplicate a shape several times with an offset (in a row, a grid, around a circle, a ring of dots), add a Repeater with layer.addShapeItem {kind: "repeater", layer} and set its Copies and its transform (position offset, rotation, scale per copy).

title: Effects (Gaussian Blur, Glow, Turbulent Displace, Fractal Noise...) are applied with add_effect
text: Effects are not commands. They are indexed as items of kind effect (find shows their id, category and parameters); the full registry is the list_effects tool (filter=<text>). Apply one with add_effect {effect: id or name, layer: id | '#n' | name, comp?, values?: {parameter id: value}}.

title: Rendering and viewing a composition
text: render_frame renders the ACTIVE composition unless you pass comp=<id>, so always pass comp. A comp is shown in the window only after comp.open {comp}. Playback: control method ui.playback {action: play|stop}; the Timeline panel: ui.panel.show {panel: Timeline}.

title: Export a composition as Lottie
text: file.exportLottie {comp, path (.json or .lottie), includeExpressions?, textAsShapes?}. Most Lottie players do not support expressions, so text driven by an expression becomes static unless the player does.

title: Rig a character or object with null joints in a script: parent first, animate after
text: When a script builds layers and parents them (layer.parent = null, or layer.setParent), parenting compensates for the parent's CURRENT transform, including keyframes and expressions it already has, so children jump. Build in two phases: create every layer and null with static transforms and set all parents first; only then add keyframes, path morphs and expressions (also on the nulls). The parenting keeps world position (it is jump-compensated).

title: Keyframing the position of a parented layer: values are in the parent's space, not comp pixels
text: Position of a layer that has a parent is in the parent's layer space (a null's anchor is [50, 50]), so comp coordinates put it in the wrong place. Read the layer's position value right after parenting, subtract the comp position it had before, and add that offset to every comp-space key. Valid while the parent chain is not rotated or scaled at rest.
keys: layer moves to the wrong place
animate a layer attached to a null

title: Pan and zoom a whole 2D scene with a camera null: key the null's anchor point, not its position
text: Parent every layer of a scene to one null at the comp centre and animate it as a camera. Zoom with its scale; pan by keying its ANCHOR POINT (anchor = point to look at - comp centre + [50, 50]) and keep its position at the comp centre, so the zoom always stays centred on screen. Panning with position moves the scale pivot off-screen.

title: Building a scene or film with hundreds of layers: run the script headless with effectcraft-cli (MCP calls stop after 60 s)
text: A run_script call through the gateway times out after about 60 s (a 400-layer scene did). For big generated builds run the same JavaScript headless: effectcraft-cli --empty script build.jsx --save-as film.ecproj (wrap each scene in (function(){...})()), preview with effectcraft-cli --project film.ecproj render-frame --comp NAME --time T --out f.png, and render with effectcraft-cli --project film.ecproj --gpu render --comp NAME --out film.mp4 --format h264. Then open the .ecproj in the app.

title: Checking whether two layers are the same in a script: compare names or indexes, not objects
text: comp.layer(i) and other lookups return a new wrapper object each time, so layerA === layerB (or !==) is never reliable: a loop that parents every layer except the camera with L !== CAM parented the camera to itself and failed with 'parenting would create a cycle'. Compare L.name or L.index instead.
keys: skip one layer in a loop

title: Keyframes seem ignored on a property with an expression: return value outside the expression's time window
text: An expression replaces the keyframed value. A gated expression such as (t>=2&&t<5) ? wobble : 0 hides the property's keyframes outside the window; return value there instead: (t>=2&&t<5) ? wobble : value. Use value + offset to add motion on top of keys.

title: Drawing paths from a script into a new comp: open that comp first (shape.newPath draws into the active comp)
text: shape.newPath (also through app.run inside run_script) adds to the ACTIVE comp and to the selected shape layer: after app.project.items.addComp call comp.openInViewer() (or comp.open), and run edit.deselectAll before each path that should get a layer of its own.
